body:
This seems to be the intended behavior.

When a state changing occurs from idle to walk, the walking animation is reset by the transition of the StateMachine and the walking animation is played from the beginning.

However, when switching between right and left, the transition does not occur since state is not changed, so the previous animation current time remains.

As a workaround, enable AllowTransitionToSelf in the StateMachine and transition to itself when the walking direction is changed in the walk state.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/432f4578-a50b-4311-98f6-06fa49fcae4a)

Other solutions are to use StateMachine instead of BlendSpace, or to reset the animation time by NodeSeek when the walking 
 direction changes.

Explain please how this is intended behavior?

1. This worked fine in all previous versions before 4.4, so why the change suddenly, why is there a breaking change? 
2. And why is it intended for method calls to not work, but other tracks work fine? 
3. Why does the method call transition work sometimes, but sometimes not?

That's inconsistent behavior and tbh I don't see reason to it. 

> However, when switching between right and left, the transition does not occur since state is not changed, so the previous animation current time remains.

It's not consistent as you describe it. Please reopen the issue.

Also, with your comment, I fail to understand what the point of a BlendSpace2D is. If it cannot do proper transitions from walking left to right. This is exactly what it was used for by the community. See countless pre 4.4 tutorials on Youtube, learned by many people. And it still works. Just not consistently and only if you are using method call tracks. Other tracks are fine.

If I set allow transition to self, then the animation is seems to be reset/started again with each tick (or whatever metric there is)

“BlendSpace” absolutely has no nuance, intent, or explanation for "Resetting" the animation.



There have been several issues sent in the past such as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/41028, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/86984, https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100009 that were definitely bugs and were fixed with an https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/100373;

Looking at the history, there was a problem in 3.x, which was fixed in 4.0 by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/48375, but the problem reappeared in 4.2. That is, the reset behavior was unintentionally included only between 4.2 and 4.3.

AnimationTree had major changes in 4.2 and 4.3, including a few compatibility breaks, and a migration manual was provided. At that time, the problem had recurred in 4.2 and was carried over to 4.3 because it was done without being noticed, and was fixed again in 4.4.

Thank you for your response. I don't understand what understanding I can take from your last comment, can you give me more context please.

Method call tracks worked perfectly between animation transitions, on 3.x and 4.x, always. I migrated my project from 3.3 to 3.4 to 3.5 to 4.2 to 4.3. In 4.4 it's bugged and only sometimes works.

Also, can you please answer my questions/respond to my observation. Specifically method call tracks not working, but other tracks working (e.g., property tracks) @TokageItLab Based on your statement I think it should not work for all track types equally.

In other words, the behavior of 4.0 and 4.1 was the correct BlendSpace/Discrete implementation, 4.2 and 4.3 were broken, and 4.4 restored it. This means that your implementation relied on a regression of a bug that occurred in 4.2 and 4.3 that was present in 3.x. So your scene should not have worked as you intended in 4.0 and 4.1.

> can you please answer my questions/respond to my observation. Specifically method call tracks not working, but other tracks working (e.g., property tracks)

First understand the difference between Discrete and non-discrete keys. https://godotengine.org/article/migrating-animations-from-godot-4-0-to-4-3/#callbackmodediscrete

Please note that "Discrete" here is the playback update timing, which is different from BlendSpace. They differ in update frequency as shown in this figure.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/67e016a1-fe82-4347-88a1-d975c60b61c7)

In other words, the properties are updated even if the animation is played from the middle of the animation; The default for AnimationTree is to have the option enabled to force the update timing to be Continuous for blending. So property tracks will be updated even if they are played in the middle of a track.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1026861b-99fa-4ddc-a001-48c38c7b413c)

However, method keys are not fired until the current time crosses the key.

Your method key is placed around 0.5 second, so if the animation is played from the beginning, the method will fire 0.5 seconds later. However, if the current time of the animation is not reset and the animation is played from around 0.6 seconds, the method key will not fire until the next loop.

Godot 3.x, 4.2 and 4.3 unintentionally reset their child animations when the closest point of BlendSpace was changed, so that the method key always played 0.5 seconds later, but this reset behavior was a bug and not existing in 4.0 and 4.1, as I explained above; This means that the definition of the correct behavior had already been done in 4.0 with breaking compatibility from 3.x, but 4.2 mistakenly reverted it. In 4.4 (and 4.3.1), it has been fixed to conform to the 4.0 and 4.1 behavior.
